report.tagline: A payments company that lets Indian businesses accept online payments, pay out money and manage cash with a few lines of code.
report.simpleSummary: When you pay on a website like Swiggy or a small D2C brand, a payment gateway sits between you and the bank. Razorpay is the most popular one in India. A business adds Razorpay to its site, and customers can pay by UPI, card, net banking or EMI. Razorpay takes a small cut of each payment and also sells tools for payouts, payroll and business banking.

overview.whatItDoes: Razorpay helps businesses collect money online and move it. Its main product is a payment gateway that accepts UPI, cards, net banking, wallets and EMIs. It also offers payment links, subscriptions, payouts to vendors, a business current account (RazorpayX), payroll and offline POS devices. It is moving into AI agents that recover abandoned carts and handle disputes.
howItWorks: A business signs up and finishes online KYC.
Developers add Razorpay checkout to their website or app using its APIs and plugins (Shopify, WooCommerce).
Customer pays; Razorpay routes the payment to the bank or card network and confirms in seconds.
Money settles to the business bank account, usually the next working day, minus Razorpay's fee.
Dashboards show payments, refunds and disputes; RazorpayX handles payouts and payroll.
Agent Studio offers AI agents for abandoned carts, failed subscriptions and disputes.
overview.valueProposition: For businesses: start accepting all payment methods in a day, with good success rates and simple developer tools, so they can focus on selling. For developers: clean APIs and documentation.

businessModel.summary: Razorpay earns a small fee on each payment it processes. It also earns from banking, payouts, payroll, POS and lending partnerships. Big clients pay lower fees; small businesses pay the standard rate.

revenueStreams.detail: A percentage of each payment, about 2% on standard plans for most domestic methods, higher on international cards.
Fees per payout and for current account and payroll features.
Device rent and transaction fees from physical stores.
Malaysia (Curlec) and Singapore, the fastest-growing part.
If a 0.4% fee on large UPI merchant payments goes live, analysts estimate ₹192 to 461 crore extra yearly revenue.

businessModel.pricing: Standard plan around 2% per transaction on most Indian payment methods and about 3% on international and some cards, with no setup fee. Large clients get custom lower rates. Check the site for current rates.
costDrivers: Fees paid to banks and card networks on every payment (the biggest cost)
Large ESOP costs (₹1,209 crore in FY25)
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a ₹1,000 card payment at a small brand. Razorpay charges about ₹20. Around ₹15 to ₹17 goes to the issuing bank and card network. Razorpay keeps about ₹3 to ₹5 before its own costs. For UPI, most payments have no merchant fee by law, so Razorpay earns very little and recovers money through other products. This is why payments is a thin-margin business: FY24 profit was only ₹34 crore on ₹2,068 crore revenue. Per-transaction splits are estimates.

growth.moat: Deep developer trust, a large share of startups and digital brands, and many connected products. Once a business runs collections, payouts and payroll through Razorpay, moving away takes months of work.

pmLessons: Developer experience can win a B2B market. Razorpay grew because engineers liked its APIs.
When the core product is thin margin, you need extra products to make money.
Regulation can wipe out a revenue line overnight. UPI zero MDR shows this.
Switching cost is a moat. Once a product is in the customer's code and finance flows, they stay.
Serve startups early and grow with them as they become big.

interviewQuestions.question: UPI has zero MDR. How would you make money from UPI payments?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explore value-added services, large-merchant MDR, faster settlement, analytics and lending. Keep small merchants free.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you improve payment success rate?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break down failures by method, bank and step. Suggest smart routing, retries and better error messages. Track success rate by segment.

interviewQuestions.question: A big client wants to cut fees by half. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Understand their volume and alternatives. Offer volume pricing, add-on value, or a mixed deal. Protect overall margin.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Razorpay build AI agents?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find painful merchant tasks (carts, disputes), check willingness to pay, start with one agent, measure revenue recovered.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Razorpay's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Successful payment volume for active businesses. Explain drivers: active businesses, success rate, volume per business, take rate.
